model: Sum of parts: core Operating PATMI capitalisation at cost of equity plus listed securities at market (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: Issued shares excluding treasury, 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 results, para (a): 847,393,232). No treasury shares, no material options outstanding; basic = diluted. Held flat: no buyback programme in use (zero repurchases FY2016-FY2025) and no planned equity issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement share-based payment add-back S$8.7m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). Already expensed inside Operating PATMI, so the stream's sbc_pct_path is held at 0 to charge it exactly once; no equity-award taxes (net-share settlement not used).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the SGD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the stream (Operating PATMI) is already after interest and after minority interests: 10y SGS ~2.4% + beta ~1.0 x ERP 5.6% = 8.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios -- risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked on the rate. No conglomerate-discount premium added: the market's NAV discount is an output to compare against, not an input.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial (lease liabilities S$5.7m at FY2025, principal repayments S$2.4m/yr). Lease cost is already inside Operating PATMI; no lease liabilities in the bridge -- one treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once by construction: the stream is Operating PATMI ATTRIBUTABLE to UOL shareholders (after the 49.63% SingLand minority and other NCI), and the securities bridge carries only UOL's attributable share of securities held inside SingLand. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.stream_definition: FY0 base S$383.7m = FY2025 Operating PATMI S$468.7m (PATMI before fair value and other gains/losses, FY2025 SGX results p.21) less UOL-attributable dividend income from FVOCI securities S$85.0m (UOB S$90.4m x 87.7% attributable share + Haw Par/OUB Centre/others ~S$5.7m; one-tier dividends are tax-exempt so pre-tax = post-tax). The dividends are stripped because their source assets are added at market in the equity_bridge (matching-asset rule). Engine mapping: 'revenue' = core attributable Operating PATMI; ebitda_margin 100%, D&A 0, cash tax 0 (PATMI is post-tax), SBC 0 (already expensed); 'capex_pct' = the share of earnings RETAINED for reinvestment (landbank replenishment, Clifford/Marina Square redevelopment capex, IP acquisitions) needed to deliver the growth path. Owner flow = distributable FCFE = core PATMI x (1 - reinvestment).
inputs.reinvestment_rationale: Ten-year group OCF-less-capex FY2016-FY2025 summed S$3.33bn (~S$333m/yr) against average Operating PATMI ~S$330m incl. dividends; on an attributable, ex-dividend basis cash conversion ran ~65-70%, i.e. ~30-35% of earnings retained, and that retention delivered ~3.6%/yr operating EPS growth (40.5c FY2016 -> 55.5c FY2025). Base holds 35% for FY2026-28 (Thomson View S$810m, Dorset Road S$524m, Hougang Central S$1.5bn JV, Novena Square stake; gearing 0.20x -> 0.26x in six months) then 30%; implied incremental ROE at terminal g 2.5% ~8%, consistent with Singapore GLS development returns.
inputs.notes: MODEL ROUTE: UOL straddles three rows of the dcf-methods routing table -- inventory-heavy developer (47% of revenue), IAS 40 fair-value investment-property owner (20%) and hotel operator (25%, held at cost) -- plus a listed-securities portfolio (2.4% of UOB) and a 50.37% listed subsidiary (SingLand). Per the skill, the parts are valued separately and summed: (1) the operating businesses (development + investment property + hotels + tech/management services, including UOL's 50.37% economic share of SingLand) as one post-interest, post-NCI earnings stream -- core Operating PATMI -- capitalised at the SGD cost of equity, net_debt held at 0 because interest on the S$4.26bn group net debt (memo) is already inside the stream; (2) the FVOCI securities at market via equity_bridge, with their dividends stripped from the stream. Reported PATMI is NOT used (fair-value swings: -S$293m FY2020 to +S$268m FY2022); Operating PATMI is the company's own audited ex-fair-value measure, as with 0004.HK's UNP. An owner-FCF DCF on group FCF was rejected: group FCF swings -S$787m to +S$812m on land purchases routed through OCF and includes 100% of SingLand. A pure NAV/P-B model was rejected as primary because NAV carries hotels at cost and IP at appraised value, neither of which the market has paid for in a decade (P/NAV ~0.40-0.83x, FY2016-2026); it is reported as a cross-check. NAV cross-check: NTA/share S$14.16 (30 Jun 2026); price 7.92 = 0.56x. SingLand is valued inside the stream at UOL's attributable earnings share rather than at its market cap. UOB holds 7.0% of UOL (cross-holding) -- no valuation effect. SBC-zero in effect: house and street bases coincide (SBC already expensed inside PATMI), so band_position collapses and should be read as null. Price note: 52-week range 7.58-11.48; the stock fell from a Feb-2026 high with the Singapore developer group, not on a UOL-specific event (no corporate action in Yahoo events other than the S$0.25 dividend, May 2026).

equity_bridge.note: Group holds ~39.84m UOB shares (FY2025 AR note 13: S$1,396.7m at Dec-2025 close S$35.06); Company directly 29.94m (S$1,049.9m), subsidiaries (mainly SingLand, 50.37%-owned) 9.89m -> attributable 34.93m x U11.SI S$41.59 (Yahoo, 2026-10-23 close) = S$1,452.6m. Singapore levies no capital-gains tax. Dividends from these shares stripped from the stream.

equity_bridge.item: Other FVOCI securities (Haw Par, OUB Centre, other unlisted), UOL-attributable
equity_bridge.note: Haw Par Company-held S$41.2m marked from S$15.68 to S$12.90 (H02.SI 2026-10-23) = S$33.9m, plus subsidiary-held share S$2.2m; OUB Centre S$52.3m at Dec-2025 book (Company-held, unlisted); other unlisted S$19.7m x 50.37% = S$9.9m.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.8% vs revenue 5yr 10.3% and operating EPS 5yr 12.5%: both comparators start from the COVID trough (FY2020 revenue S$1.98bn, operating EPS 30.8c), so they overstate trend growth. The nine-year operating EPS CAGR FY2016-FY2025 is 3.6%, matching the equity CAGR -- that is the trend the model leans on.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use Operating PATMI per share (basic EPS before fair value and other gains: FY2016 40.5c, FY2020 30.8c, FY2022 40.9c, FY2025 55.5c), because statutory EPS (FY2020 1.6c) is dominated by revaluations. FCF CAGRs on the owner series (group OCF - capex - SBC - interest income): FY2020 S$360.4m -> FY2025 S$531.4m; the 3yr base (FY2022) is negative (-S$102.9m reported, land purchases), so undefined. SBC is ~0.3% of revenue and does not distort the series. FY2025 operating EPS of 55.5c is ~50% above the FY2016-2024 average (~36c): the base case treats part of that as cyclical.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +12%: H1 FY2026 core (Operating PATMI less attributable dividends) ~S$212.6m vs ~S$161m in H1 FY2025; with 2H held near 2H FY2025's ~S$223m, FY2026 core ~S$430-438m. FY2027-28 give back ~7% as the Pinetree Hill / Watten House / MEYER BLUE recognition wave rolls off before Thomson Reserve (launch 4Q2026), Dorset Gardens (1H2027) and Hougang Central (2H2027) reach recognition, and as interest on the higher post-acquisition debt bites. From FY2029 The Clifford (completion 2028) and NoMad Hilton add recurring income and growth settles at Singapore nominal GDP-like 2-2.5%.
base.capex_note: Reinvestment share of earnings; see inputs.reinvestment_rationale.
base.cap_note: 15x distributable FCFE (~10.5x core earnings) -- a mid-cycle Singapore developer P/E. Gordon at 8.0%/2.5% is 18.6x, so the cap binds: the model does not grant the Gordon multiple to a cyclical developer.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2025-26 Singapore residential upcycle (10,815 new-home sales in 2025, ABSD unchanged) delivers a record FY2026, then development profit normalises as the current recognition wave completes and the replenished landbank (Thomson View, Dorset Road, Hougang Central) is launched at moderating price growth of 3-4%/yr. Singapore office stays resilient on tight CBD supply, offsetting weak UK/Australian office occupancy; hotels grow moderately under manpower-cost pressure. The Clifford (2028) and asset-light PPHG fee growth add recurring income. Marina Square SDI is treated as a long-dated option, not in the numbers. Core earnings end the decade ~10% above FY2025 and the market keeps paying a mid-cycle developer multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: Lower rates keep Singapore household demand strong through the next three launches, sold at healthy margins; Marina Square SDI moves from Written Permission to a phased hyper-mixed-use redevelopment that adds residential sales and lifts recurring rent from an under-used downtown asset; The Clifford leases up at Grade-A CBD rents; PPHG's management pipeline (~1,463 rooms in SE Asia) compounds fee income with little capital. Lower reinvestment intensity (higher incremental returns) and an 18x exit multiple (still below the 20.6x Gordon multiple at 8%/3%) reflect a partial closing of the NAV discount.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns: renewed price spikes trigger further cooling measures, or a correction leaves the 2025-26 land bought at full GLS prices (Hougang Central S$1.5bn) earning thin margins. UK office occupancy (already ~50% at 110 High Holborn/120 Holborn) and Australian office stay weak and drag rents and valuations; gearing that rose from 0.20x to 0.26x is refinanced at higher rates with fixed cover down to 66% and a 2-year average maturity; China residential (THE PUYUAN) disappoints. Core earnings fall ~20% from the FY2026 peak to roughly the FY2016-24 average and retention rises to 38-40% just to hold the landbank. Exit at 12x FCFE (~7.5x earnings).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because FY2025-26 earnings sit at a cyclical high for Singapore residential and the bear path is simply mean reversion to the FY2016-24 average, not a distress case. Base 50%. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- sustained upcycle, Marina Square SDI execution and NAV-discount compression.

valuation_philosophy.summary: UOL is valued as what an outside minority shareholder actually owns: a claim on the attributable, post-interest, ex-revaluation earnings of a Singapore developer-landlord-hotelier, less what must be retained to keep the landbank and portfolio growing, plus a liquid UOB stake worth its market price. The S$14.16 book NAV is a cross-check, not the answer -- the hotels are at cost, the investment property at appraisal, and management has shown no intent to liquidate, so the NAV discount is a persistent feature, not a mispricing that closes by itself.
valuation_philosophy.nav_cross_check: NTA/share S$14.16 at 30 Jun 2026; P/NAV at current price 0.56x. Historical P/NAV ~0.40x (2024 low) to ~0.83x (Feb-2026 high, S$11.48 vs S$13.88).
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates and the cap binds in every scenario: the exit multiple, not the discount rate, is the main lever.
FY0/FY2026 core earnings sit near a cyclical peak; the base already assumes a ~7% give-back but a deeper or longer residential downturn would cut further.
The UOB stake (~S$1.45bn, ~S$1.71/share) is marked at today's UOB price; a 20% fall in UOB moves IV by ~S$0.34/share.
Reinvestment share (30-40%) is inferred from ten years of cash conversion, not guided; at 25% throughout the base value rises roughly 7-10%.
Marina Square SDI and hidden hotel revaluation upside are not in the base numbers; a sale or REIT spin-off of hotels at market would crystallise NAV the model does not count.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 7.58-11.48. UOB (U11.SI) and Haw Par (H02.SI) marked from the same API, same close.
data_sources.financials: U14.SI_Metrics.csv (core_metrics) and kpis; Operating PATMI from FY2025 SGX full-year results (Quarterly_FY2025-SGXFinStatement.txt lines 86, 1292) and H1 FY2026 results (HalfYear_H1-2026.txt lines 83, 1034); securities from FY2025 AR Investments page (line 2026) and note 13 (line 8291); share count and borrowings from H1 FY2026 results (lines 142, 648).
